relations.subject: backup:archived-repository
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - promoted predicate; same triple already established in backup-service.json ('the Backup Service cannot perform further backups to the repository'), independently re-evidenced here from the REST operation's own page with a wider exception list (retrieve information, restore data, examine data - all still permitted)
relations.evidence: This means that no further scheduled or manually triggered tasks can be run on the repository; with the exception of those that _retrieve information_, _restore data_, and _examine data_.

relations.subject: backup:archived-repository
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: minted - cannotRevertTo. The registry's negation predicates (doesNotSupport, doesNotAffect) describe a bounded incompatibility or a deliberately-untouched dependent, not a ONE-WAY lifecycle transition. This page states the archive operation is irreversible as a flat fact, independent of any specific follow-on action, which is a distinct shape worth its own predicate rather than stretching doesNotSupport to cover it.
relations.evidence: Note that a repository that has been archived _cannot_ be returned to active state.

notable_absence.finding: This page states the Full Admin requirement only inline in the curl-syntax prose ('The username and password must identify an administrator with the Full Admin role'), unlike backup-get-cluster-info.md, backup-get-expired-backups.md, backup-get-plan-info.md and backup-get-repository-info.md, which each carry a dedicated '## Required Permissions' section header naming a disjunction of THREE roles (Full Admin / Backup [Full] Admin / Read-Only Admin). Every write-shaped operation in this batch (archive, create, delete, examine) follows this page's pattern - one role, no dedicated section - while every read/list-shaped operation follows the other. The port number 8097 appears repeatedly in this page's own curl examples (e.g. ':8097/api/v1/cluster/self/') but is never named as 'the Backup Service port' the way backup-get-expired-backups.md and backup-get-repository-info.md do explicitly ('These URIs are only available from the Backup Service port (8097 by default)') - so the port concept is minted on those pages, not here, even though the number appears here first in this batch's read order.

cross_component_finding: This page's own exception list for an archived repository - 'the exception of those that _retrieve information_, _restore data_, and _examine data_' - names, by function, exactly the three REST operations covered by backup-get-repository-info.md, backup-restore-data.md (batch B) and backup-examine-data.md (this batch, file 7 below): the page's prose and the REST API's own endpoint catalogue independently agree on what 'read-only against an archived repository' means. See backup-create-repository.json for this round's fuller treatment of the core question posed for this round (whether the Backup Service REST API's repository/plan objects are the SAME construct as cbbackupmgr's, per round 11's already-promoted finding).
